question: Members of the Citizens party (Renew) condemned the French winegrowers’ boycott of Spanish products at the border between the two countries in a written question to the Commission in October 2023 (E-003107/231). French farmers regularly block and ransack lorries, and Spain has been lodging complaints2 for years, none of which have put a stop to this unacceptable violence.

In late January 2024, French farmers not only prevented the free movement of Spanish products across Europe once again, but also boasted to the press about violent and illegal acts they had committed, such as dumping Spanish wine onto the road, setting fire to fruits and vegetables, etc.

3 As if that were not enough, the French Government asked law enforcement not to intervene4, thereby legitimising the breakdown of the European legal order. In its answer to written question E-003107/23,5 the Commission stated that it had asked the French authorities to take measures to prevent further attacks on the principle of free movement of goods. 1.
What precise measures did the Commission ask the French authorities to take to prevent further disruptions of this kind?
What measures is it going to call for this time?
How is the Commission going to ensure compliance with Council Regulation (EC) No 2679/98?6
